content.overview: Section 17 lists documents that must be registered, including gifts of immovable property, non-testamentary instruments creating or extinguishing rights of Rs 100 or more in immovable property, and leases from year to year or for more than one year.
content.study: Compulsory registration is the gateway rule. Pair it with section 49 (effect of non-registration) and with TPA formalities such as sale and lease. An unregistered document caught by section 17 generally cannot affect the property or prove the transaction, subject to the section 49 proviso.

Statutory check 2026-10-03 against India Code bitstream 123456789/2190, Registration Act, 1908. Section 17(1) requires registration of: (a) instruments of gift of immovable property; (b) other non-testamentary instruments creating, declaring, assigning, limiting or extinguishing a right, title or interest of Rs 100 or more in immovable property; (c) non-testamentary instruments acknowledging consideration for such a transaction; (d) leases from year to year, for any term exceeding one year, or reserving a yearly rent; (e) non-testamentary instruments transferring or assigning a decree, order or award that creates or extinguishes such a right of Rs 100 or more. Section 17(3) also requires registration of authorities to adopt a son executed after 1 January 1872 and not conferred by a will. Local note matched (a), (b) and part of (d). It omitted (c), (e), yearly rent, and adoption authorities. State amendments not checked.
